attempted_claim: Let C_{2,2} be the class of orientable complete finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds with exactly one connected totally geodesic boundary component of genus 2 and exactly two toric cusps. Let W be the unique (up to homeomorphism) manifold in the Frigerio-Martelli-Petronio class M_{2,2} (complexity 4), with V_0 = vol(W) = 4*Vol(Delta^{id}_{pi/6}). Prove that vol(N) >= V_0 for every N in C_{2,2}, with equality iff N is homeomorphic to W, and determine the sharp constant delta* > 0 such that no N in C_{2,2} has vol(N) in (V_0, V_0 + delta*) while delta* is best possible, identifying the manifold(s) attaining V_0 + delta*. Establish this by SL(2,C) character-variety trace identities and Hodgson-Kerckhoff / Neumann-Zagier Dehn-filling volume estimates combined with Kojima-decomposition / Miyamoto polyhedral volume bounds.
decisive_failure: Target work was blocked before any complete proof: the sharp gap delta* and extremal identification need certified large-scale enumeration with interval-arithmetic volume certification plus uniform geometric-limit control for genus-2 geodesic-boundary manifolds, none available in-session with the bare-mpmath stack. Only routine blocking diagnostics were produced; no verified theorem, extremal value, or certifiable computation is claimed.
